name: PullToRefresh
summary: Mobile-only refresh-on-pull gesture wrapper. Detects a downward drag at the top of a scroll container, expands a Spinner-bearing reveal area, and fires onRefresh when the user pulls past the threshold. Auto-collapses when the consumer resolves the refresh. Distinct from button-driven refresh (use a Refresh IconButton in the Toolbar).

onRefresh.description: Async function. Resolves when the refresh is complete; the gesture collapses after.

threshold.description: Px pull distance to commit. Below: cancel and snap back. Above: fire onRefresh.

indicator.description: arrow: an arrow rotates as the pull progresses (Apple HIG). spinner: just renders Spinner once committed.

label.description: Optional 'Pull to refresh' / 'Release to refresh' / 'Refreshing…' label under the indicator.

keyboard: R (when scroll container is focused) - alternative refresh trigger
rules: Per WCAG 2.5.7 — pull-to-refresh MUST have a non-drag alternative. Render a Refresh IconButton in the Toolbar OR document the 'R' keyboard shortcut.
Honor prefers-reduced-motion: skip the arrow rotation; snap to the indicator position.

do: Pair with a Refresh IconButton fallback in the Toolbar.
Use the arrow indicator on iOS-flavor apps.
Resolve onRefresh as quickly as possible — past 5 s, surface a Toast 'Still refreshing…' so the user knows the gesture took.
dont: Don't use PullToRefresh on desktop — there's no gesture model that maps cleanly.
Don't use PullToRefresh inside nested scroll containers — the gesture races with the inner scroll.
Don't reset the scroll position on refresh — preserve it.

changelog.note: Initial PullToRefresh contract. Arrow + spinner indicators. WCAG 2.5.7 non-drag fallback required.
